sn12.15:1.1: While the Exalted One was at Savatthi
sn12.15:1.2: the venerable Kaccāyana of that clan came to visit him, and saluting him sat down at one side. So seated he asked the Exalted One, saying:—
sn12.15:1.3: Lord, we hear the phrase 'right view, right view.'
sn12.15:1.4: Now how far is there a 'right view'?
sn12.15:2.1: This world, Kaccāyana, usually bases [its view] on two things: on existence and on non-existence.
sn12.15:2.2: Now he, who with right insight sees the uprising of the world as it really is, does not hold with the non-existence of the world.
sn12.15:2.3: But he, who with right insight sees the passing away of the world as it really is, does not hold with the existence of the world.
sn12.15:2.4: Grasping after systems, imprisoned by dogmas is this world, Kaccāyana, for the most part.
sn12.15:2.5: And the man who does not go after that system-grasping, that mental standpoint, that dogmatic bias, who does not grasp at it, does not take up his stand upon it, [does not think]:—'It is my soul!'
sn12.15:2.6: who thinks: 'that which arises is just Ill, that which passes away is Ill'—this man is not in doubt, is not perplexed. Knowledge herein is his that is not merely another's.
sn12.15:2.7: Thus far, Kaccāyana, he has right view.
sn12.15:3.2: Nothing exists:—this is the other extreme.
sn12.15:3.3: Not approaching either extreme the Tathagata teaches you a doctrine by the middle [way]:—
sn12.15:3.4: Conditioned by ignorance activities come to pass,
sn12.15:3.5: conditioned by activities consciousness; thus conditioned [arises] name-and-shape; and sense arises, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, decay-and-death, grief, suffering, ...
sn12.15:3.6: even such is the uprising of this entire mass of ill.
sn12.15:3.7: But from the utter fading away and ceasing of ignorance [arises] ceasing of activities,
sn12.15:3.9: of this entire mass of ill.
